chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'A man did not purify his wealth (pay Zakat), so his Zakat was taken at the time of his death and paid. Would that suffice for him?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes.' I said, 'And if he bequeathed a bequest from his third, and Zakat had not been paid on it, would it suffice for him from his Zakat?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes. Zakat is reckoned for him, and no optional (Zakat) is upon him, and upon him is the obligatory (Zakat).'
ai.seo_question: Does paying Zakat from a deceased person's estate after their death suffice for their religious obligation?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the settlement of Zakat obligations for the deceased, establishing that payment from the estate suffices even if omitted during life. It further distinguishes between obligatory Zakat and voluntary (Nafil) charity, noting that while the mandatory duty is fulfilled, the deceased does not accrue reward for Nafil acts unless specifically bequeathed, highlighting the Shia juristic view on the hierarchy of estate deductions.
